evidence.locus: shelfmark, age and contents rows pp.61,71,83,197–279

stages.label: Benevento VI.33 notated Missal
stages.limitations: Catalogue aliases 938/1299/6276 are not separate books; no complete text or rite-wide use established.
stages.reception: Benevento holding and apparent origin do not prove every local church used its text.
stages.scope: One manuscript with indexed Mass cycles and Canon.
stages.summary: Usuarium identifies the shelfmarked manuscript and its indexed Mass components.
stages.witness_label: Benevento Chapter Library Cod. VI.33

evidence.claim: The report identifies the same twelfth-century manuscript under VI.29 and Egerton 3511.
evidence.locus: announcement paragraphs identifying century, missal genre and two shelfmarks

stages.label: Benevento VI.29 Missal
stages.limitations: Provenance and Beneventan script do not establish historical liturgical use or old-rite identity.
stages.reception: Chapter custody is established; medieval local use remains unproved.
stages.scope: One twelfth-century Missal manuscript, formerly BL Egerton 3511; contents uncollated.
stages.summary: Government custody account and catalogue resolve two shelfmarks to one manuscript.
stages.witness_label: Benevento VI.29 = former BL Egerton 3511

evidence.claim: A specific 1480 Messina Missal copy is identified.

stages.label: 1480 Messina Missal print
stages.limitations: No original page or first-use evidence; Gallicorum is title language, not ancient Gallican rite identification.
stages.reception: Book title names Messina; church-level reception unknown.
stages.scope: Edition-identified local Missal print; original body uninspected.
stages.summary: Usuarium identifies an exact Manchester holding with a Messina title and 1480 date.
stages.witness_label: Missale Messanense, John Rylands Library 18620

evidence.claim: The title identifies the local book and advertises sanctoral/common correction.

stages.label: 1499 Messina Missal print
stages.limitations: Advertising does not verify a predecessor or exact changed reading.
stages.reception: No adoption by all Messina churches proved.
stages.scope: Indexed temporal, sanctoral, common, ordinary, Canon and rubrics.
stages.summary: A 1499 Venetian print for Messina is identified with an indexed Mass-book structure.
stages.witness_label: Missale Messanense, Catania Agatina Inc.1

evidence.claim: A specific 1538 Messina Missal edition is catalogued.
evidence.locus: original title, age, Naples shelfmark and Acireale copy remark

stages.label: 1538 Messina Missal print
stages.limitations: Two holdings do not establish two states; no comparison with 1499 or normative act inspected.
stages.reception: Present Naples and Acireale holdings do not prove historical use there.
stages.scope: Edition-identified local Missal print; text not collated.
stages.summary: Usuarium identifies the 1538 print and a Naples copy, with a second copy at Acireale.
stages.witness_label: Missale Gallicanum et Messanensis Ecclesie, BN Napoli S.Q.21.D21

evidence.claim: Venice 1550 is printed on the title.
The named formulary and texts are visible on the identified folios.

stages.label: Venice witness before the Xavierre revision
stages.limitations: This does not reconstruct the full 1550 missal, identify its immediate exemplar, or establish how long each house used it.
stages.reception: The title identifies the Dominican use. A printed intended-use statement does not prove reception in every province.
stages.scope: Suscepimus Deus formulary within the temporale.
stages.summary: Suscepimus Deus appears under Dominica octava, with Deus cuius providentia as collect and Attendite a falsis prophetis as Gospel.
stages.witness_label: Missale ad usum fratrum Praedicatorum Sancti Dominici, Venice, 1550

evidence.claim: Printing dated 1604, under Hieronymus Xavierre.
The editor explicitly describes conformity of Epistles and Gospels to Roman use.
The revised combination is directly visible.

stages.label: Xavierre revision witnessed in the Rome printing
stages.limitations: The original intervention predates this printing; 1604 is not assigned as the first promulgation or first revised edition. Only the selected formulary is text-collated.
stages.reception: Clement VIII’s brief dated 2 April 1602 preserves the Order’s rite while authorizing conformity in specified matters. Its adoption windows depend on place and availability of copies; actual local uptake is not established.
stages.scope: A revised temporale formulary and the revision’s reprinted authorizing documents.
stages.summary: Suscepimus Deus now has Largire nobis as collect and the unjust-steward Gospel, with its heading moved to Dominica sexta after the octave of Trinity.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta ritum sacri ordinis Praedicatorum S. P. N. Dominici, Rome, ex typographia Alfonsi Ciacconi, apud Carolum Vulliettum, 1604

evidence.claim: Imprint is Venice, Giunta, 1574; the book identifies the Carmelite observance and custom of Jerusalem.
These printed entries are directly visible.

stages.label: Carmelite October calendar before the later additions
stages.limitations: Calendar absence on one date is not proof that a saint or devotion is absent from every section of the volume.
stages.reception: This is the Carmelite Latin book identified by its own title. The title’s Jerusalem claim is recorded without constructing a genealogy from it.
stages.scope: Printed October calendar.
stages.summary: October 5 has no printed feast. October 6 includes Abraham, Isaac and Jacob with three lessons and the octave of Michael; October 8 includes Simeon the prophet.
stages.witness_label: Missale antique professionis Regularium beatissime Dei genitricis semperque virginis Marie de Monte Carmelo, Venice: Giunta, 1574

evidence.claim: The 1621 printing is described as printed again, with chapter and Prior General authority.
Teresa’s feast and common-Mass reference are printed, distinct from marginal handwriting.
The instrument is dated 26 September 1584, not 1621.

stages.label: Carmelite calendar with Teresa of Jesus
stages.limitations: Neither the exact introduction date of Teresa’s feast nor the date of the chapter decree is established. Manuscript corrections in this copy are excluded.
stages.reception: The printed book belongs to the Carmelite ancient-observance sequence. A handwritten direction to a Discalced missal on p. 409 is not treated as the printed rite’s prescription.
stages.scope: Printed October calendar and Teresa’s printed common-Mass reference.
stages.summary: October 5 prints Teresa as duplex minus with a commemoration of Placidus and companions. Teresa’s sanctoral entry directs the reader to the common Dilexisti iustitiam Mass.
stages.witness_label: Missale fratrum Carmelitarum Ordinis Beatae Dei Genitricis Mariae de monte Carmelo, Venice: Giunta, 1621

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1538 witness.
Colophon and comparison identify this state.
The colophon dates publication decimo septimo kalendas Augusti 1538 (16 July); names Galharde and corrector Fernandus Olegarius; expressly lists corrections, additions and omissions.
evidence.locus: Colophon fol. 184v, PDF 364; preceding recto foliation on PDF 363

evidence.claim: Seven prayer units are visible: Omnipotens…in diluvio, Petimus te, Deus cuius filius, Deus qui dispersa congregas, Domine Iesu Christe, Benedic Domine hos ramos, Omnipotens Iesu Christe; the preface begins Qui miro dispositionis ordine.

stages.label: Galharde’s revised Braga printing before Limpo
stages.limitations: The 1538 colophon describes its own revision without identifying the exact previous printing as an immediate parent. The earlier state has not been directly collated. This surviving copy is incomplete; the whole digital file is acquired, not the complete original printed volume.
stages.reception: A book of the church of Braga; surviving print identification does not establish continuous archdiocesan use until 1558.
stages.scope: Directly inspected Palm Sunday blessing and the printing’s own account of corrections and additions.
stages.summary: The colophon reports corrected passages, added Gloria/Credo rules and Masses of Christian victory and St Apollonia, preface notation following Coimbra cathedral practice, and removal of some material already available in the Manual. The Palm blessing has seven prayers and one preface.
stages.witness_label: Missale Bracarense, Lisbon: Germão Galharde, 1538; BNP RES-1633-A

evidence.claim: Identifies the 1558 witness.
Describes concrete revisions.

stages.label: Limpo’s revised Braga missal
stages.limitations: Primary leaves were not reached; no word-for-word collation is claimed.
stages.reception: Revision for Braga. Limpo’s Carmelite membership does not establish derivation from a Carmelite missal; Carvalho rejects direct dependence on the Carmelite 1551 and Lyon 1556 books he compared.
stages.scope: Reported changes to the Ordo and Palm Sunday blessing.
stages.summary: Limpo’s revision changes the Ordo and Palm Sunday blessing.
stages.witness_label: Missale juxta usum et ordinem Almae Bracarensis Ecclesiae, Lyon: Petrus Fradin, 1558; BnF B-1478

evidence.claim: Identifies the revised 1924 Vatican printing.
The dateline is 8 December 1924; it directs the archdiocese’s priests to this missal.
The decree dated 9 December 1924 declares the edition typical and sets the future conformity and feast-insertion rules.

stages.label: Braga typical edition approved in December 1924
stages.limitations: These rules describe the 1924 state; their absence from 1558 has not been established. Later inserted feasts in this copy must not be assigned to 1924.
stages.reception: The bull requires this missal for priests of the Archdiocese of Braga. This establishes the contemporary prescription, not universal subsequent observance or present law.
stages.scope: The title edition and its binding approval/conformity rules; no complete body reconstruction.
stages.summary: Approved 8 December and declared typical 9 December 1924. Future Holy See changes to Masses already contained in it must be applied; newly imposed universal feasts must enter the Braga calendar.
stages.witness_label: Missale Bracarense, Rome: Typis Polyglottis Vaticanis, 1924; title edition distinct from the digitized copy’s later supplements

evidence.claim: Describes the preparation from the Ordinarium and states that the 1603 missal does not print these preparation texts.

stages.label: Carthusian preparation in the 1582 Ordinarium
stages.limitations: Primary leaves not directly inspected. Their omission from a missal is not treated as omission from the liturgy or a ritual revision.
stages.reception: An identified order-level prescription or scholarly description does not establish use in every charterhouse.
stages.scope: Reported preparatory prayers and gestures in the complementary Ordinarium.
stages.summary: Preparation begins at the Gospel side with Pone Domine and a short Confiteor; the confession includes omissione and three strikes of the breast.
stages.witness_label: Ordinarium Cartusiense, Paris, 1582

evidence.claim: Prints the Gloria word order and title with chapter 1602 and imprint 1603.

stages.label: Paris missal following the 1602 chapter
stages.limitations: USUARIUM 8356 links Google Books UxFlAAAAcAAJ, whose complete download returned HTTP 429. The 1582 Ordinarium is complementary evidence, not a demonstrated parent version.
stages.reception: An identified order-level prescription or scholarly description does not establish use in every charterhouse.
stages.scope: Reported Gloria wording and title authority.
stages.summary: The Gloria reads propter gloriam tuam magnam. The cited title invokes the general chapter held in 1602; 1603 is the publication year.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cartusiani Ordinis, Paris: Iametius Mettayer, 1603

evidence.claim: Chapter year 1622 and Lyon printing 1627 are explicit.
The named Ordinary prayer loci and rubrics are directly image-checked.

stages.label: Lyon witness authorized by the 1622 chapter
stages.limitations: The legacy cartusiense-1620 identifier remains for stable references only. No complete Ordinary transcription and no intervening change from 1603 is inferred.
stages.reception: An identified order-level prescription or scholarly description does not establish use in every charterhouse.
stages.scope: Title and printed Ordinary prayers on pp. 203–205.
stages.summary: The title invokes the chapter of 1622. Gloria retains propter gloriam tuam magnam; the water prayer begins De latere Domini, the chalice offering uses In spiritu humilitatis, and Orate asks prayer pro me peccatore.
stages.witness_label: Missale Cartusiani Ordinis, Lyon: Ioannes Pillehotte, 1627; BSB 2 Liturg. 197

evidence.claim: Dates and identifies Latin MS 24 as a mid-thirteenth-century Salisbury manuscript.
Identifies C and distinguishes its base Ordinary/calendar from late additions.

stages.label: Crawford missal before the later vesting additions
stages.limitations: The numeric bounds encode the identified century, not a claim of use throughout it. No universal Sarum inception date is inferred, and later added prayers are not dated to the base hand.
stages.reception: A Sarum book, with Legg recording its own closing identification of the use; no claim that every Sarum church used an identical Ordinary.
stages.scope: The base Ordinary and calendar of Legg’s manuscript C.
stages.summary: Veni Creator belongs at the beginning of Mass. The relics feast is entered on 15 September and Corpus Christi is absent from the base book. Prayers for individual vestments in a vacant space are a much later hand.
stages.witness_label: Sarum Missal, John Rylands Library Latin MS 24; Legg manuscript C

stages.date_label: First quarter of the fourteenth century

evidence.claim: Identifies and dates B; distinguishes the later calendar annotation and describes the Ordinary difference.

stages.label: Bologna manuscript’s vesting and offertory arrangement
stages.limitations: The annotation is later than the base hand and has no independently verified insertion date. C and B are compared witnesses, not a demonstrated immediate parent and revised child.
stages.reception: The editor suggests an Oxford destination from a Frideswide formulary; this remains his inference, not a new provenance finding.
stages.scope: The Ordinary in Legg’s manuscript B, with added calendar directions kept distinct.
stages.summary: Individual vestment prayers accompany preparation, while Veni Creator occurs at the offertory. A later calendar annotation directs the relics feast to the Sunday after the July translation of Thomas of Canterbury, while its service remains at the September position.
stages.witness_label: Sarum Missal, Bologna University Library MS 2565; Legg manuscript B

evidence.claim: Identifies the manuscript, local dedication and Dubricius Mass, and prints its second-Lent-Sunday Secret variant.

stages.label: Whitchurch manuscript with local Dubricius observance
stages.limitations: The manuscript is incomplete, including substantial Holy Week and Canon losses. The feast’s presence in a local book does not prove that it was obligatory across the diocese.
stages.reception: Henderson identifies the original church as Whitchurch, Monmouthshire, from its dedication to Dubricius.
stages.scope: Selected calendar and Mass proper features in Henderson’s University College manuscript.
stages.summary: The calendar marks the local dedication on 11 March and Dubricius on 14 November; a Dubricius Mass is present. For the second Sunday of Lent Henderson reports the Secret Sacrificiis praesentibus, Domine.
stages.witness_label: Hereford-use Whitchurch missal, University College Oxford; Henderson’s fourteenth-century manuscript

evidence.claim: Transcribes the 1 September 1502 imprint and episcopal/chapter authority claim.
Reports the Dubricius difference and allows the manuscript Secret to be compared with the printed base text.

stages.label: Hereford printing represented by Henderson
stages.limitations: The 1502 original is mediated by Henderson’s critical reprint. The witness difference does not identify when or why the prayers diverged, nor prove a diocesan decree removing a local feast.
stages.reception: The printed title reports bishop, dean and chapter authority; geographical uptake remains unestablished.
stages.scope: Selected proper differences from the Whitchurch manuscript.
stages.summary: The printed second-Sunday-of-Lent Secret is Ecclesiae tuae, Domine, munera placatus assume. Henderson reports that the manuscript’s Dubricius Mass is absent from the printing.
stages.witness_label: Missale Herfordense, Rouen: Pierre Olivier and Jean Mauditier for Jean Richard, 1502; represented by Henderson 1874

evidence.claim: Lists the early prints and describes their limited differences and continuing shared errors.

stages.label: York’s closely related printed witnesses
stages.limitations: This bounded witness group is not one complete reconstructed book or five independently proved recensions. The first print is undated; c. 1509 is the editor’s attribution. His proposed manuscript ancestry is explicitly tentative.
stages.reception: Printed intended use is York. Henderson describes substantial earlier manuscript ceremonial diversity, so the printed state must not be projected backwards to all medieval York books.
stages.scope: Henderson’s bounded comparison of five printed editions.
stages.summary: The earliest printing lacks the monthly calendar notices and places Modus finiendi Collectas and Considerationes circa Missam differently. Henderson reports shared errors across the sequence, including an omitted Holy Saturday rubric line and Petrocius placed in April rather than June; musical note lengths also vary.
stages.witness_label: York missals: Violette, undated c. 1509; Gachet 1516; Bernard/Cousin 1517; Gachet 1530; Regnault 1533

evidence.claim: Identifies the main volume and dates the witness 1320–1341.
States the earlier repertory and compares it with the fifteenth-century witnesses.

stages.label: Notated missal’s larger medieval repertory
stages.limitations: The manuscript is incomplete and composite surviving material must be mapped carefully. Its fuller repertory may include options rather than mandatory observance of every listed item.
stages.reception: A medieval Esztergom exemplar; no claim that every listed saint or sequence was used in every celebration.
stages.scope: Preparation placement and proper/sequence repertory compared by Déri with 1484.
stages.summary: Déri counts approximately 210 saints with special propers and 78 sequences in the fourteenth-century notated missal. It also includes the Pentecost-octave Mass and the Transfiguration grape blessing that his later comparators lack. Preparation follows the Holy Saturday baptismal order.
stages.witness_label: Missale notatum Strigoniense ante 1341; main volume AM Bratislava EC Lad 3, with related surviving material

evidence.claim: Reproduces the 31 August 1484 colophon, printer and chapter/vicar authority.
Describes preparation placement, sanctoral reduction and sequence comparison.

stages.label: Esztergom’s 1484 printed repertory
stages.limitations: The 1484 book is not identified as the moment when all differences first arose. Déri expressly requires more complex relationships than a single subtraction/addition sequence; the Pálóczi comparator already shares much of the later state. The absent intervening preparation texts could be a copying omission or assumed memorized text, not a proven ritual abolition.
stages.reception: The colophon identifies Esztergom use and the vicar and chapter’s assent; survival of a printing does not demonstrate uniform implementation.
stages.scope: Selected repertory and arrangement changes reported in Déri’s edition.
stages.summary: Compared with the pre-1341 witness, the special-proper sanctoral is reduced by about one third. The later sequentiary retains 39 of the earlier 78 sequences and adds ten others; its material substantially agrees with the intervening Pálóczi manuscript. Preparation prayers move to the beginning of the book.
stages.witness_label: Missale Strigoniense, Nuremberg: Anton Koberger, completed 31 August 1484; Déri’s critical text

evidence.claim: Lists separate 1774 ordinary, 1775 sacramental ritual and 1775 rites-and-lections titles.
Describes prayer, ritual and calendar additions associated with the first printed Taksa.

stages.label: First Roman printed ordinary and lection collection
stages.limitations: No original 1774/1775 page comparison. The two Eucharistic books are not two successive revisions. The retrospective does not securely assign every item to an individual volume.
stages.reception: Prepared for Malabar Catholic worship; no claim that every reported addition originated in 1774.
stages.scope: Complementary Eucharistic volumes; the sacramental ritual is excluded.
stages.summary: The official retrospective reports received Maronite prayers, Latin-derived vesting and Holy Week material, and altered calendar/readings.
stages.witness_label: Ordo Chaldaicus Missae Beatorum Apostolorum (1774); Ordo Chaldaicus rituum et lectionum (1775)

evidence.claim: Explicitly names Propaganda printings of 1775 and 1845 and describes the earlier arrangement.
Calls the Masses approved on 31 July 1905 newly appended after comparison with the exemplar; only their prior absence is inferred.

stages.label: Propaganda exemplar named as 1845
stages.limitations: Propers scope is limited to the reported absence of the newly appended 1905 Masses, not a complete proper inventory. Documented as a named exemplar, not an independently identified physical edition or a proven substantive revision of 1775. Do not equate it with the separately reported 1844 lection book or 1845 sacramental ritual.
stages.reception: An authorized editorial exemplar for the 1906 Malabar book; its actual historical use is not reconstructed.
stages.scope: Bounded earlier arrangement and absence of the later-approved appended Masses, as described in the 1904/1905 permissions.
stages.summary: The permission describes an exemplar with dispersed ordinary material and Rogation readings in a supplement.
stages.witness_label: Missale Syro-Chaldaeo-Malabaricum, Propaganda printing dated 1845 by the 1904 permission

evidence.claim: Directs collection of the ordinary and relocation of Rogation readings.
Reports comparison with the exemplar and newly appended Masses approved by the Congregation of Rites on 31 July 1905.
evidence.locus: Physical PDF 6, 15 October 1905 approval and 1906 imprint

evidence.claim: The reproduced 10 August 1905 official reply reports the Rites 31 July nulla osta for the requested insertion.
Opening native entries identify Francis Xavier (3 December), Nicholas (6 December), Ambrose (7 December), Holy House (10 December) and Lucy (13 December).

stages.label: Reorganized travel missal with appended Masses
stages.limitations: The added section is located and its first named feasts are checked. Remaining feast and votive entries are not fully enumerated or transcribed; the older appendix 1*–54* is not all attributed to the 1905 permission.
stages.reception: Aloysius Pareparambil petitioned also on behalf of the other two Syrian apostolic vicars. Propaganda’s reply reports the Rites nulla osta for insertion; the 15 October 1905 imprimatur authorizes printing. Neither record establishes universal actual adoption.
stages.scope: Andreas Kalapura edition: arrangement and additions explicitly described in its permissions.
stages.summary: Collects the ordinary, moves the three pre-Septuagesima Rogation readings into place, and adds the 1905-authorized Masses in a distinct 55*–101* section, beginning with December feasts.
stages.witness_label: Ordo chaldaicus rituum et lectionum, Puttenpalli, Mar Thoma Sliha Press, 1906

evidence.claim: Describes the edition against which Vadakel’s changes are stated.

stages.label: Roman exemplar described by the 1946 editor
stages.limitations: No date or exact Roman printing is named. This contextual state cannot be merged with the 1845 exemplar without further evidence.
stages.reception: Malabar liturgical exemplar, not the Latin Roman Missal; the phrase Roman Edition indicates printing context here.
stages.scope: Only features explicitly contrasted by the 1946 foreword.
stages.summary: Prayers/rubrics were dispersed; some feasts appeared only in the calendar; server prayers were merely indicated; Marian Huthama was absent.
stages.witness_label: Unidentified Roman edition named in Augustine Kandathil’s foreword to Vadakel 1946

evidence.claim: Dates the printing and explicitly describes the changed content and arrangement.
evidence.locus: Physical PDF 2–4, title, foreword and contents

evidence.claim: Names Holy See letter Prot. 2521/28 of 3 September 1930 for double-asterisk feasts and the Immaculate Conception Gospel.

stages.label: Vadakel’s corrected and expanded arrangement
stages.limitations: Bodies of the ordinary, propers and appendix are absent from the excerpt. No direct descent from the 1906 book is asserted. The 1930 act is reported in the book, not independently inspected.
stages.reception: Approved by Augustine Kandathil in the foreword dated 13 May 1946; catalogue’s 1945 date is not followed.
stages.scope: Editorial arrangement and specified additions verified in original preliminary leaves.
stages.summary: Regroups and brackets transferred material, supplies proper and server texts, and preserves a Nineveh appendix with Marian Huthama.
stages.witness_label: Ordo Chaldaicus rituum et lectionum, reditus a P. Matthaeo Vadakel, Mar Thoma Sleeha, Alwaye, 1946

evidence.claim: Identifies the Latin consultative text and its component page ranges.

stages.label: Latin study text for restoration
stages.limitations: Book not acquired. Publication in 1955 is distinct from approval on 26 June 1957 and reception in 1962.
stages.reception: Roman commission study text; not asserted to have been used as a Latin-language altar missal.
stages.scope: Consultative formulation of the original reform, not a lay translation lineage.
stages.summary: Contains the common order, three anaphoras and forms of celebration for episcopal consultation.
stages.witness_label: Liturgia Siro-Malabaresi: Revisione e Ristampa del Messale Siro-Malabarese, Rome 1955, Prot. 947/48

evidence.claim: Distinguishes the approved three-anaphora programme, companion books, and narrower 12 May 1960 Syriac printing.
Lists the three books as publications of the restoration.

stages.label: Restoration issued in complementary books
stages.limitations: No original Latin 1959 or Syriac 1960 pages acquired. The CMS file labelled 1959 is a 1998 translation. Companion volumes must not become sequential whole-missal revisions.
stages.reception: Programme approved by Pius XII in 1957; its complete contents were not all introduced in worship in 1962.
stages.scope: Rubrics/calendar, propers and a restricted Syriac ordinary issued separately.
stages.summary: The three books supply different components; the Syriac ordinary includes only Addai and Mari in the simple form.
stages.witness_label: Ordo celebrationis Quddasa (Rome 1959); Supplementum Mysteriorum (Rome 1960); Taksa d’Quddasa (Alwaye 1960)

evidence.claim: Separates 20 January promulgation from 3 July introduction and identifies omitted components.
Identifies bilingual publication and continuing Syriac passages.
evidence.locus: RR-122/JT description, paragraphs on Syriac prayers and promulgation

stages.label: Partial restoration introduced in worship
stages.limitations: A reception stage, not a new original-language revision inferred from translation. Original instruction and complete book not inspected.
stages.reception: Syro-Malabar episcopal introduction; not proof of uniform practice in every parish.
stages.scope: Community reception of the restricted restored order in the approved 1962 Syriac–Malayalam Qurbana book; its operative Malayalam text is received service-book language, while this stage remains limited to the partial restoration introduced in worship.
stages.summary: The bishops introduced the bilingual order on 3 July; several approved restored components remained unimplemented.
stages.witness_label: The Order of Qurbana of the Syro-Malabar Church, Alwaye 1962, Syriac and Malayalam

evidence.claim: Confirms year, typical-edition designation and native Syriac content.
evidence.locus: Physical PDF 3–5, English/Syriac title leaves and first rubric leaf

stages.label: 2003 Syriac typical-edition witness
stages.limitations: Do not count as an established substantive new stage solely from the title. No full book, approval decree or changed-text statement obtained.
stages.reception: Title says use of the Church of the East Syrians of Malabar; Catholic bibliographic context corroborated by commission-hosted source list.
stages.scope: Confirmed printing; substantive state and predecessor comparison unresolved.
stages.summary: Title identifies the Malabar use and Addai–Mari anaphora; native Syriac leaves are visible.
stages.witness_label: Order of the Mysteries with the First Hallowing of Mar Addai and Mar Mari, Editio Typica, Rome 2003

evidence.claim: Reassembles gatherings of O across the three shelfmarks; the print also uses other material.

stages.label: Manuscript O before Roman editing
stages.limitations: Reconstruction attributed to Jabbour; surviving manuscripts and colophon not inspected. It is not a complete uncontested single-parent genealogy.
stages.reception: Maronite manuscript provenance; date of its dispatch to Rome is disputed. The later printed uniform formula must not be projected back over all manuscript layers.
stages.scope: Source manuscript identified by Jabbour, including the pre-editing institution and epiclesis layers; not all precursors of the print.
stages.summary: A divided 1566 missal used in preparing the first print; supplements also contributed.
stages.witness_label: Mikhail al-Rizzi’s manuscript O: Florence BNCF Cl.III.79 and Cl.III.74, with Vatican Vat.sir.431; colophon BNCF Cl.III.74 f 154r–v.

evidence.claim: Latin 1594 and Syriac 1592 dates coexist in this physical witness; 1594 dedication and examiner colophon are visible.
Describes fourteen anaphoras and alteration of institution and epiclesis.
Identifies Sixtus first and the inclusion of Sharar.

stages.label: First print with revised institution and epicleses
stages.limitations: Liturgical body not transcribed or collated. Dual title dates do not establish two successive textual states.
stages.reception: Dib reports introduction at the 1596 synod with Dandini. Beggiani records initial prohibition and later permission while manuscript formulas continued locally; neither account proves universal immediate replacement.
stages.scope: Roman first printing, bounded by checked paratext and source-described liturgical revision.
stages.summary: Fourteen anaphoras; Sixtus first and Sharar included. Institution wording standardized; epiclesis petitions altered.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum iuxta ritum Ecclesiae nationis Maronitarum, Romae in Typographia Medicea; IA bub_gb_5Eqy8WGF9aQC.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes alpha copies marking names from beta copies substituting them.
Confirms a 1608 reimpression with textual changes and new Du Perron preface.

stages.label: Reprint variant replacing commemorated names
stages.limitations: No 1608 copy independently collated. Jabbour warns that editions may be impressions; alpha/beta is his analytical grouping, not a new universal liturgical edition.
stages.reception: Presence in surviving copies establishes a printed variant; no community-wide reception date established.
stages.scope: Specific diptych/commemoration revision in Jabbour’s beta group; not every 1608 copy.
stages.summary: One 1608 group substitutes Maron, Antony, Jacob and Ephrem for earlier commemorated names.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum 1608 reimpressions, beta group in Jabbour’s comparison; BnF RES M-B-3 is a separately identified 1608 reissue, not assigned here to beta.

evidence.claim: Reports altered roster, fourteen total, Roman Church and Sharar-derived Good Friday order.
Explains adaptation of Roman Canon material to the structure of Twelve Apostles.

stages.label: Roman-derived anaphora and Good Friday adaptation

evidence.claim: Title identifies edition; James correction and diptych-conclusion removal are explicitly described.
Lists retained/new selection and rejected titles; retains the later six-part diptych arrangement in Twelve Apostles rather than newly introducing it.
Describes fraction, feast/prayer, dismissal, Presanctified and other changes.
Describes Arabic parallel prayers, solemn rubrics, canon-derived admonitions and optional prayers before/after Mass.
Patriarch’s decree dated 8 December 1922 prescribes the edition for his patriarchate and wherever his rite is observed.

stages.label: Rahmani’s revised altar missal
stages.limitations: These are primary-described changes, not independent before/after Syriac collation. The editor’s authorship/confessional diagnoses are not adopted as modern critical conclusions. His statement about no alteration to institution narrative/epiclesis is narrower than “no changes to anaphoras.” The six-section Twelve Apostles diptychs are an explicitly retained feature, not a new 1922 innovation. The James manuscript-reference footnote is malformed as printed and needs shelfmark disambiguation.
stages.reception: Issued by Syriac Catholic patriarch Ignatius Ephrem II Rahmani. The decree makes this edition alone authentic within his stated jurisdiction/rite; it does not legislate for all West Syriac churches or prove universal actual adoption.
stages.scope: Revised Syriac Catholic celebrant book with selected anaphoras, ordinary/prayer changes, Presanctified rite, rubrics and Arabic parallel public prayers.
stages.summary: James is revised against older manuscripts and Greek; John Evangelist is followed by Twelve Apostles, Basil of Caesarea, Mark, Eustathius and Cyril of Jerusalem. The editor suppresses Peter/Xystus and rejects three 1843 attributions. He removes conclusions after individual James diptychs; replaces the fraction/consignation formula with “Panem coelestem frangimus”; restores entrance prayers and changes Holy Thursday/Holy Saturday and dismissal prayers. The Presanctified rite is replaced, and solemn-celebration rubrics and preparatory/concluding prayers are added. Arabic is printed beside appropriate Syriac public prayers.
stages.witness_label: Missale iuxta ritum Ecclesiae Apostolicae Antiochenae Syrorum auctoritate recognitum; Ketābā de-taksā de-qūrrābā; Typis Patriarchalibus in Seminario Sciarfensi de Monte Libano, 1922
